title: Composition of the counit-defined tensor transposes on systems
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $\mathscr N_W$ be the category of normalized strict semilinear derived $((A_n)_W)_n$-systems with finite-Tor constructible levels as in [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Use the simultaneous pullback, tensor and adjunction models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For $h=f,g,gf$ let $F_h\dashv G_h$ be the section adjunctions of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates], choosing the specified finite realizations of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Write $\epsilon_h$ for their counits, $\alpha:F_gF_f\simeq F_{gf}$ for the compact-support comparison [thm-sf-comp-composition], and $c:G_{gf}\simeq G_fG_g$ for its adjunction conjugate [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. All tensor and projection maps below are the specified system maps [def-exchange-projection, lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence], not separately chosen lifts of finite-level maps. Assume their projection maps are invertible on the displayed inputs. All objects below are assumed to lie in these categories.

Set $\Omega_h=G_h\mathbf1$, where $\mathbf1_W=((A_n)_W)_n$ is the coefficient unit on $W$. Define $\theta_{h,L}:h^*L\otimes\Omega_h\to G_hL$ to be the adjoint transpose of
$$\sigma_{h,L}:F_h(h^*L\otimes\Omega_h)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{sym}}F_h(\Omega_h\otimes h^*L)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{h,\Omega_h,L}^{-1}}F_h\Omega_h\otimes L\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{h,\mathbf1}\otimes1}L,$$
including unit identifications, as in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Assume $\rho=\theta_{f,\Omega_g}$ is invertible, set $W=f^*\Omega_g\otimes\Omega_f$, and put $\mu=\rho^{-1}c_{\mathbf1}:\Omega_{gf}\simeq W$. For every $K\in\mathscr N_Z$, the following maps from $(gf)^*K\otimes W$ to $G_fG_gK$ are equal:
$$A_K=c_K\circ\theta_{gf,K}\circ(1\otimes\mu^{-1}),\qquad B_K=\theta_{f,G_gK}\circ(f^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1_{\Omega_f}),$$
where $B_K$ includes the pullback/tensor reassociation $(gf)^*K\otimes W\simeq f^*(g^*K\otimes\Omega_g)\otimes\Omega_f$.

More precisely both have, under $F_gF_f\dashv G_fG_g$, the same transpose
$$F_gF_f((gf)^*K\otimes W)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{sym},\,\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}}F_gF_fW\otimes K\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}\mathbf1_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,$$
where $t=\epsilon_{g,\mathbf1}\circ F_g(\sigma_{f,\Omega_g})$ and
$$\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}=F_g(\mathrm{PF}_{f,W,g^*K})\circ\mathrm{PF}_{g,F_fW,K}.$$
All associators, pullback composition and unit identifications are the canonical ones of the same simultaneous models. The equality holds in the derived strict-system category before total inverse limit; no orientation by a twist, smoothness, or faithfulness of general derived evaluation is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $H=F_gF_f$ and let $s$ denote tensor symmetry. It is convenient to put
$$Q_{h,L,M}=s_{F_hM,L}\,\mathrm{PF}_{h,M,L}^{-1}\,F_h(s_{h^*L,M}).$$
Thus $Q_{h,L,M}:F_h(h^*L\otimes M)\to L\otimes F_hM$. By naturality of the specified projection maps [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence], $Q$ is natural in both inputs. Put $e_h=\epsilon_{h,\mathbf1}$. Naturality of symmetry and the unit constraints rewrites the definition in the statement as
$$\sigma_{h,L}=(1_L\otimes e_h)Q_{h,L,\Omega_h}.$$
In particular $\sigma_{h,-}$ is natural: for $a:L\to L'$, substitute $(a\otimes1)Q_{h,L,\Omega_h}=Q_{h,L',\Omega_h}F_h(h^*a\otimes1)$ and then compose with $1\otimes e_h$. All notation refers to the actual simultaneous section maps, whose tensor and transpose constructions are supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

proof.text:
The section adjunction transpose is $u\mapsto\epsilon_{h,L}F_h(u)$ by [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]. The composite counit from [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] is
$$e^{H}_L=\epsilon_{g,L}F_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gL}):HG_fG_gL\to L.$$
Since $c$ is the conjugate of $\alpha$, changing adjunctions gives
$$e^{H}_L H(c_L)=\epsilon_{gf,L}\alpha_{G_{gf}L}.$$
Also $\sigma_{f,\Omega_g}=\epsilon_{f,\Omega_g}F_f(\rho)$ by the defining transpose of $\rho$. Hence the $t$ in the statement is $e^{H}_{\mathbf1}H(\rho)$. Using $c_{\mathbf1}\mu^{-1}=\rho$ and naturality of $\alpha$ now gives
$$\epsilon_{gf,\mathbf1}F_{gf}(\mu^{-1})\alpha_W=e^{H}_{\mathbf1}H(c_{\mathbf1}\mu^{-1})=t.$$
These are equations of section maps, not equations checked only on evaluations.

proof.text:
Put $D=(gf)^*K\otimes W$. Taking the transpose of $A_K$ using Step 2, then naturality of $\alpha$, yields
$$\begin{aligned}
A_K^\flat
&=e^{H}_K H(c_K)H(\theta_{gf,K})H(1\otimes\mu^{-1})\\
&=\sigma_{gf,K}F_{gf}(1\otimes\mu^{-1})\alpha_D\\
&=(1_K\otimes[\epsilon_{gf,\mathbf1}F_{gf}(\mu^{-1})])Q_{gf,K,W}\alpha_D.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses the formula of Step 1 and naturality of $Q$ in its third argument [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence]; $\mu^{-1}:W\to\Omega_{gf}$ has exactly that type. Here $Q_{gf,K,W}$ is defined: naturality of the projection maps in their first input [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence] along the isomorphism $\mu^{-1}:W\to\Omega_{gf}$ gives $\mathrm{PF}_{gf,W,K}=F_{gf}(\mu\otimes1)\,\mathrm{PF}_{gf,\Omega_{gf},K}\,(F_{gf}(\mu^{-1})\otimes1)$, and $\mathrm{PF}_{gf,\Omega_{gf},K}$ is invertible since it occurs in $\theta_{gf,K}$. The transpose formula is the one in [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates].

proof.text:
Define
$$Q_{H,K,W}=Q_{g,K,F_fW}\,F_g(Q_{f,g^*K,W}):HD\to K\otimes HW.$$
Invert the projection-composition equation of [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence] at $(M,N)=(W,K)$ and insert the symmetries in the definition of $Q$. It gives
$$Q_{gf,K,W}\alpha_D=(1_K\otimes\alpha_W)Q_{H,K,W}.$$
For clarity, expansion of $Q_H$ cancels the adjacent factors $F_g(s_{g^*K,F_fW})F_g(s_{F_fW,g^*K})$ and gives
$$Q_{H,K,W}=s_{HW,K}\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}H(s_{(gf)^*K,W}).$$
Naturality of $\alpha$ moves the input symmetry through it; naturality of the output symmetry moves it through $\alpha_W$. No symmetry compatibility of $F_h$ as a monoidal functor is being presumed. Combining this equation with Steps 2 and 3 shows
$$A_K^\flat=(1_K\otimes t)Q_{H,K,W}.$$
Expanding $Q_H$ and canceling the intermediate symmetry twice identifies it with tensor symmetry followed by $\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}$ and the final symmetry $HW\otimes K\to K\otimes HW$. Thus this is precisely the common transpose displayed in the statement.

proof.text:
Set $T=g^*K\otimes\Omega_g$ and $a=\theta_{g,K}:T\to G_gK$. The reassociation in $B_K$ identifies $D$ with $f^*T\otimes\Omega_f$. Under the composite adjunction its transpose is
$$\begin{aligned}
B_K^\flat
&=\epsilon_{g,K}F_g\bigl(\sigma_{f,G_gK}F_f(f^*a\otimes1)\bigr)\\
&=\epsilon_{g,K}F_g(a)\,F_g(\sigma_{f,T})
=\sigma_{g,K}F_g(\sigma_{f,T}).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is the naturality proved in Step 1, applied to this actual section morphism $a$, and the last is the counit formula for the transpose of $\theta_{g,K}$. Here $\sigma_{f,T}$ is defined because $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,T}$ is invertible: apply [lem-pur-system-projection-tensor-associativity] with $h=f$, $L=g^*K$, $L'=\Omega_g$, $M=\Omega_f$; its two invertibility hypotheses are $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,\Omega_g}$, which occurs in $\rho=\theta_{f,\Omega_g}$, and $\mathrm{PF}_{f,W,g^*K}$, a factor of the displayed $\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}$, and it concludes that $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,g^*K\otimes\Omega_g}$ is invertible. Naturality of $\sigma_{f,-}$ at $a$ uses this and the invertibility of $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,G_gK}$, which occurs in $\theta_{f,G_gK}$. [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] supplies that formula and the section counits, and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] supplies the composite counit.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-system-projection-tensor-associativity] for $h=f$, $L=g^*K$, $L'=\Omega_g$ and $M=\Omega_f$. Its two invertibility hypotheses, $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,\Omega_g}$ (in $\rho$) and $\mathrm{PF}_{f,W,g^*K}$ (a factor of $\mathrm{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}$), are among the displayed inputs; its conclusion supplies the invertibility of $\mathrm{PF}_{f,\Omega_f,T}$ needed for $\sigma_{f,T}=(1_T\otimes e_f)Q_{f,T,\Omega_f}$, as already used in Step 5. Its equation and Step 1 give, writing $b=\sigma_{f,\Omega_g}:F_fW\to\Omega_g$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_{f,T}
&=(1_{g^*K}\otimes1_{\Omega_g}\otimes e_f)(1_{g^*K}\otimes Q_{f,\Omega_g,\Omega_f})Q_{f,g^*K,W}\\
&=(1_{g^*K}\otimes b)Q_{f,g^*K,W}.
\end{aligned}$$
The canonical pullback tensor comparison in that lemma is exactly the reassociation used in $B_K$. This is the tensor-variable identity missing from mere naturality or composition coherence of the projection maps.

proof.text:
By naturality in the third input of $Q_g$ [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence],
$$Q_{g,K,\Omega_g}F_g(1_{g^*K}\otimes b)=(1_K\otimes F_gb)Q_{g,K,F_fW}.$$
Substitute Step 6 into Step 5 and use $\sigma_{g,K}=(1_K\otimes e_g)Q_{g,K,\Omega_g}$. This gives
$$B_K^\flat=(1_K\otimes e_gF_gb)Q_{g,K,F_fW}F_g(Q_{f,g^*K,W})=(1_K\otimes t)Q_{H,K,W}=A_K^\flat.$$
The hom-set adjunction bijection of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates], applied twice, is injective. It therefore gives $A_K=B_K$ and the claimed formula for their common transpose. Every equality was obtained within the section category; inverse limits and faithfulness of derived evaluation are unnecessary.
